tasks.short: Translate customer needs into requirements for custom machinery.

steps.what: Review customer requirements, the opportunity record and existing equipment specifications.
Discuss operating conditions, constraints and acceptance criteria with the customer.
Assess feasibility with engineering and identify unresolved design assumptions.
Write the engineering brief, distinguishing confirmed requirements from assumptions and open questions.

loop.input: Requirements source pack, discovery notes, acceptance criteria and feasibility notes.
loop.output: Engineering brief with source references, assumptions and open questions.
loop.check: Validate required fields and units; the sales engineer checks every requirement against its source.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per brief; unresolved conflicts return to the sales engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the brief, but free-text notes need interpretation without inventing design requirements.

steps.what: Send the approved brief to engineering and record outstanding questions.

tasks.design: An integration assembles a source pack from the {CRM} and {DOCS}; a structured brief separates requirements, assumptions and acceptance criteria. A bounded drafting loop fills narrative sections with source references, and the sales engineer approves the brief before the {WORKFLOW} creates the engineering handoff in the {PROJECT}. Customer discovery and engineering feasibility discussions remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer context and engineering constraints lived in separate records and informal discussions. A template alone could not interpret inconsistent notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces, structured brief templates and bounded text drafting make the paperwork feasible to automate. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort, but does not establish technical feasibility.
tasks.still_hard: Novel machinery, incomplete operating data and conflicting acceptance criteria still require engineering judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Find the unstated operational need and recognise when an apparently small requirement changes the machine design.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less brief assembly and more customer discovery. The sales engineer can offer a requirements readiness review, while engineering retains design approval rights.

reach.role: sales representative of technical and scientific products
reach.task: Qualify customer requirements before requesting engineering support.
reach.learn: Learn operating constraints, measurable acceptance criteria and the limits of standard configurations.

evidence.claim: Rule-based configuration and quoting can handle established equipment constraints.
Meyn's documented quoting case supports automation of repeatable configuration work, not novel machinery design.
Source-linked brief drafting can reduce assembly work while leaving feasibility decisions with engineering.

assumptions: This describes a typical machinery supplier with separate sales and engineering roles.
Time shares are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors, not measured customer data.
The first build covers one machinery family and one brief template.
GDPR applies to personal data in customer notes; access follows existing confidentiality restrictions.
EU AI Act literacy duties apply to staff using the model; applicable national rules govern employee consultation.
The access range includes consultation where required; formal processes may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which machinery families have approved configuration rules?
Who can approve requirements and who can commit engineering capacity?
Can the customer requirements and equipment specifications be accessed through supported interfaces?
Which employee consultation requirements apply locally?
research_questions: Which brief fields can be populated directly without a model?
What source checks catch omitted constraints and incorrect units?
Does brief preparation account for enough time to justify integration?
new_work: Review drafted requirements and source references.
Resolve conflicting customer and engineering statements.
Maintain brief fields, unit checks and interface mappings.
Evaluate drafts when machinery specifications change.

tasks.short: Help customers and colleagues use, operate and maintain equipment.

steps.what: Log the support request and link the customer and equipment record.
Ask the requester about symptoms, operating conditions and previous actions.
Find applicable operating instructions, maintenance guidance and previous support cases.

loop.input: Support context and approved manuals filtered by equipment model and revision.
loop.output: Relevant passages, source references and explicit information gaps.
loop.check: Verify source existence, equipment applicability and revision; retain original warnings alongside passages.
loop.stop: One retrieval and one extraction pass; missing or conflicting guidance returns an evidence gap.
loop.why_not_simpler: Metadata filters identify manuals, but varied symptom descriptions need a bounded text-matching step.

steps.what: Explain suitable actions and check the requester understands their limits.
Arrange specialist support or a service visit when advice is insufficient.
Record advice, actions and follow-up commitments in the support ticket.

loop.input: Sales engineer's notes, support advice and service referral.
loop.output: Ticket update separating advice, completed actions and future commitments.
loop.check: The sales engineer checks action status, equipment identity and commitments before saving.
loop.stop: One draft per interaction; incomplete notes remain flagged for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need interpretation; direct copying cannot reliably distinguish advice from completed actions.

tasks.design: Configure intake, equipment links and referral routes in the {HELPDESK}, connected to the {CRM}. A bounded lookup over approved material in the {DOCS} prepares evidence for the sales engineer, who gives the advice; a second bounded loop drafts the ticket update for approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice depended on context held by experienced staff, while manuals and case histories were difficult to search together.
tasks.enabler_now: Equipment metadata, helpdesk routing and source-linked text extraction can shorten preparation and recording without replacing the support conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete descriptions, obsolete manuals and unsafe customer interpretations require experienced intervention.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt the explanation to the requester's skill and recognise when remote advice should stop.

ambition.what: Guided first-use support for small customers without maintenance specialists

tasks.altitude: The sales engineer spends less time finding instructions and recording calls, freeing time for guided first-use sessions. Advice and escalation rights stay within the existing service policy.

reach.task: Explain service coverage and route equipment support requests.
reach.learn: Learn warranty boundaries, escalation thresholds and how to avoid unsupported technical promises.

evidence.claim: Source-filtered support preparation and configured routing are feasible, but their value depends on manual quality.
Verint Wrap Up Bot demonstrates writing call summaries into customer records.
The AXA Health case documents reduced after-call work in a service desk; it does not establish equipment-support performance.

assumptions: The task includes customer and internal requests; the steps illustrate a customer case.
Time shares are estimates; conversation remains the largest component, consistent with the supplied priors.
The first release uses written notes and does not require call recording.
GDPR requires an appropriate basis, restricted access and retention controls for personal support records.
EU AI Act literacy duties apply; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
If call recording or staff-monitoring analytics are later introduced in the Netherlands, works council consent requirements need assessment under [S12].
The access range includes applicable consultation, whose elapsed duration may be longer.
unknowns: Are manuals current and linked to equipment revisions?
Which advice requires a qualified service engineer?
Are warranty and service coverage rules recorded consistently?
What access and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can metadata and ordinary search satisfy most evidence lookups before adding a model?
How often do relevant manual passages omit necessary warnings or context?
What prevents service referrals from being routed correctly?
new_work: Review support record drafts and referral decisions.
Maintain equipment-to-manual mappings and escalation routes.
Resolve retrieval gaps and outdated guidance.
Sample evidence packs for missing warnings and incorrect revisions.

tasks.short: Investigate faults in installed equipment and agree the next action.

steps.what: Review equipment configuration, service history and reported symptoms.
Ask the operator when the fault occurs and what changed beforehand.
Inspect equipment and perform authorised tests using diagnostic instruments, the {OTHER} category.
Compare findings with fault guidance and evaluate possible causes.

loop.input: Observed findings and approved fault guidance for the equipment revision.
loop.output: Evidence table linking observations to documented causes, contradictions and missing tests.
loop.check: Check model and revision deterministically; the sales engineer verifies cited passages and applicability.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass; absent evidence or contradictions return to manual investigation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed fault trees handle coded alarms, but narrative observations require text interpretation.

steps.what: Decide the likely cause and agree repair, further testing or specialist escalation.
Document the diagnosis and hand the action plan to the service team.

tasks.design: A read-only integration assembles equipment and service history from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HELPDESK}. Deterministic fault checks handle coded observations, while a bounded lookup in the {DOCS} prepares an evidence table for human diagnosis; approved structured findings populate the diagnostic report and service referral.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment histories were fragmented, and many faults depended on observations that were never captured consistently.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured test records and supported exports can automate preparation and reporting. Bounded text extraction can organise manual evidence without assuming a breakthrough in fault diagnosis.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults, physical inspection, safe testing and causal judgement remain expensive and situational.
tasks.human_edge: Notice abnormal behaviour, test competing explanations and know when evidence is insufficient to resume operation.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less history retrieval and report assembly, but most diagnostic work remains. No new repair authority or equipment-release rights are granted.

reach.role: sales representative of technical and scientific products
reach.task: Collect useful fault details before handing a case to technical support.
reach.learn: Learn equipment identification, symptom timelines and the distinction between observations and diagnoses.

evidence.claim: History retrieval, deterministic fault checks and report generation can assist diagnosis without automating physical investigation.
The digest contains no documented case establishing autonomous diagnosis of installed equipment.

assumptions: The sales engineer performs only tests permitted by existing competence and service procedures.
Time shares are estimates; physical and conversational investigation dominate, consistent with the supplied priors.
The first build covers one equipment family and reads records without controlling equipment.
Approved diagnostic findings are structured before report generation.
GDPR applies where service records identify people; customer equipment information also needs contractual access controls.
EU AI Act literacy duties apply, and employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
The access range includes consultation where required; customer site access can add elapsed delay.
unknowns: Which tests may the sales engineer perform?
Who authorises repair and return to operation?
Are equipment configurations and service histories complete?
Which fault codes have validated deterministic diagnostic rules?
Can customer equipment data be accessed remotely?
research_questions: Which recurring faults can be handled with approved fault trees alone?
Can evidence tables expose contradictory observations reliably?
How much preparation and reporting time is actually available to save?
new_work: Review evidence tables for wrong equipment revisions and unsupported links.
Maintain fault-code mappings and approved test procedures.
Handle missing service histories and inconsistent identifiers.
Validate report templates against actual diagnostic handoffs.

tasks.short: Write and release accurate technical product documentation.

steps.what: Collect approved specifications, drawings, change notes and existing documentation.
Clarify missing technical facts and intended readers with engineering.
Draft technical descriptions and instructions using approved sources and document templates.

loop.input: Approved source pack, scope, clarifications and document template.
loop.output: Draft with source references, generated tables and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Validate units, identifiers and references; reuse approved warnings verbatim and flag unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per section; unresolved gaps go to the technical reviewer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables and standard sections are deterministic, but reader-facing explanations require bounded language drafting.

steps.what: Review technical accuracy, instructions, warnings and document applicability before approving release.
Publish the approved revision and update document links for customers and colleagues.

tasks.design: Configure approved-source collection and revision control in the {DOCS}. An artefact generator fills tables and standard sections deterministically, then a bounded loop drafts explanations with source references; the technical reviewer approves the release, which the {WORKFLOW} publishes and links to equipment records in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications, drawings and change notes were difficult to assemble, and ordinary templates did not write coherent explanations.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled source packs, deterministic document generation and bounded drafting can remove much of the assembly and writing work. Technical review remains necessary.
tasks.still_hard: Missing engineering facts, safety instructions, conflicting revisions and specialist terminology still require careful review.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a reader can use the instructions correctly and recognise a technically plausible but unsafe explanation.

ambition.what: Customer-specific commissioning guide for the delivered equipment configuration

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling and writing documents to clarifying gaps and improving usable instructions. The sales engineer can prepare commissioning guides, while release authority remains with the technical reviewer.

reach.task: Prepare equipment demonstrations using released technical instructions.
reach.learn: Learn instructional sequencing, configuration applicability and when a demonstration needs specialist supervision.

evidence.claim: Templates and structured specifications support deterministic technical document generation.
Bounded drafting from approved sources can assist explanatory prose, with technical release review.
The digest provides no product or documented case specifically establishing technical documentation performance.

assumptions: The first build covers one document family and one language.
Time shares are estimates; document production dominates, consistent with the supplied priors.
The reviewer remains responsible for approval; automatic publishing consumes that recorded approval without requesting it twice.
Generated drafts may increase review effort initially; the review allocation is not assumed to shrink.
GDPR applies to personal data in sources, and proprietary engineering material remains access-controlled.
EU AI Act literacy duties apply; applicable national rules govern employee consultation.
The access range includes consultation where required; formal processes may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Who approves safety instructions and publication?
Which customer configurations can be represented with structured fields?
Which languages and document formats are required?
What restrictions apply to processing engineering material?
research_questions: Which sections can use approved text unchanged?
How reliably do source checks detect unsupported technical claims?
Does generated prose increase reviewer workload?
Can readers complete commissioning steps using the proposed guide?
new_work: Review generated explanations and resolve flagged source gaps.
Maintain templates, approved warnings and terminology.
Update source mappings after engineering changes.
Check rendering, revision links and publication permissions.

role.altitude: Sales engineers spend less time assembling technical context, briefs and records, and more time on customer discovery, safe advice and engineering trade-offs. Engineering approval, service authorisation and document release rights remain with their designated roles.
reach: Help sales representatives of technical and scientific products collect better requirements and fault details.
Help sales representatives of services explain coverage and route support requests.
Help demonstrators and product promoters use accurate, configuration-specific instructions.
skills_to_grow: Write measurable requirements and acceptance criteria.
Distinguish observations, assumptions and confirmed technical facts.
Review source-linked drafts for omitted constraints and unsafe wording.
Structure equipment metadata, revision links and reusable document fields.
Explain technical limits clearly to customers and adjacent sales roles.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a connected technical readiness service: a pre-design requirements review, guided first-use support and a configuration-specific commissioning guide. Pilot it for one equipment family, with engineering and service teams retaining their existing approval rights.
